summary: This is a Makefile snippet that sets up a help command. When you run `make help` or just `make` with no arguments, it clears the screen and displays a formatted list of all available commands by parsing special comments in the Makefile itself. The yellow color constant is defined but not used in this snippet.

explanations.1: SHELL:=bash sets the shell that Make will use to execute commands to bash instead of the default sh.
explanations.5: COLOR_YELLOW:=33 defines a variable storing the ANSI color code for yellow text, though it's not actually used in this snippet.
explanations.8: .PHONY: help tells Make that 'help' is not a real file to create, just a command to run.
explanations.12: @clear runs the clear command, and the @ symbol prevents Make from printing the command itself to the screen.
explanations.14: @awk is using awk (a text processing tool) to parse the Makefile and find all targets that have ## comments; it formats them nicely with colors and prints them. The $$ is how you escape a dollar sign in a Makefile so awk receives a literal $.
explanations.16: @echo "" prints a blank line at the end for spacing.
